title: partner-listing-rollback-and-incident-runbook-wip
content:
Purpose:
This working runbook captures proposed operational playbooks, communication templates, and minimum technical checks for rolling back a partner listing or handling marketplace listing incidents (AWS, GCP, Azure). Intended audience: Marketplace PMs, Partner Ops, Partner Success, Customer Support, SRE, and Legal.

Scope / When to use this document:
- Rolling back a listing because of critical security issues (credentials leak, broken auth).
- Rolling back due to severe billing or metering defects causing customer double-billing or incorrect entitlements.
- Emergency content removal for legal/compliance takedown requests.
- Marketplace listing causing platform-wide latency or error spikes (e.g., SDK hooks causing traffic storms).
- Any incident where customers are materially impacted or where a public notice is required.

Quick decision rubric (use at triage):
- Severity: Are customers experiencing data loss, billing harm, or security exposure? If yes -> immediate rollback.
- Scope: Are >5% of customers affected or >1 enterprise account? Rollback recommended.
- Reversibility: Is change reversible without state corruption? If yes -> rollback; if no -> escalate with engineering.
- Legal hold: Is there a takedown notice? Legal + CISO approval required within 1 hour.

Pre-launch hardening checklist (must be done before any listing goes live):
- Billing & Metering: Verify SKU mapping end-to-end with test purchases in each cloud marketplace sandbox. Capture screenshots.
- Auth & Credentials: Confirm keys/secrets are not embedded in listing artifacts (images, copy, attachments). Run secret-scan on all assets.
- Rollback playbook present: Link to runbook, Slack channel, and on-call rotation.
- Smoke tests: Automated smoke test passing against the listing APIs and provisioning flows.
- Contact list: Partner PM, Partner Success lead, Support lead, Legal owner, SRE on-call, and Marketplace partner rep.
- Canary policy: Has canary window and traffic split been defined? If not, require hold.

Monitoring signals to watch (alerts + dashboards):
- Marketplace provisioning failure rate > 3% (10m avg).
- Billing instrumentation anomaly: token_count mismatch or invoice delta > 5% between expected vs observed.
- Error budget burn rate > 50% within 30m after listing change.
- Sudden surge in support tickets mentioning the listing + keywords: "overcharged", "not provisioned", "data leak".
- External reports: Security vulnerability report submitted to security@redwood.com.

Triage roles & responsibilities (first 60 minutes):
- Incident Commander (IC): PM owning the listing (usually Partner PM) - declares rollback/hold.
- Technical Lead (TL): Eng SRE or Partner integration engineer - runs diagnostics and executes rollback steps.
- Communications Lead (Comm): Partner Success - drafts messaging and coordinates with Support and Sales.
- Legal/CISO: Rapid review for legal takedown or disclosures.
- Support Liaison: Support manager - preps canned responses and case routing.

Immediate actions (first 30m):
1) IC: Post to #marketplace-incidents Slack channel with subject: [INCIDENT] <listing-name> - suspected listing issue. Include one-line summary and a link to this runbook.
2) TL: Pull logs: provisioning logs, billing telemetry, marketplace webhooks. Snapshot and attach to JIRA-GTM-987.
3) Comm: Prepare a short notice for partners/customers (see templates below).
4) IC + TL: Decide rollback vs pause. If severity rubric met, move to rollback.

Rollback run (technical) — cross-cloud common steps:
- Step 0: Confirm backups: Ensure we have recent backup of configuration artifacts (listing metadata, SKU mappings, attachments).
- Step 1: Toggle marketplace visibility flag (if supported) to remove offering from search/listing. Prefer reversible hide over full deletion.
- Step 2: Disable any automated provisioning webhooks that create customer instances. Put a feature-flag/kill-switch to immediately reject new provisioning calls with 503 and a clear error code.
- Step 3: For billing metering issues, ring-fence incoming billing events by inserting a filter to forward to a dead-letter queue and issue a hold in the billing pipeline for the affected SKU(s).
- Step 4: Revert last commit/tag used by listing deployment (if listing assets are hosted by Redwood) or re-upload previous artifact version to marketplace console. Document exact artifact ID and timestamp in the incident ticket.
- Step 5: Apply temporary entitlement rollback: for cloud marketplaces that propagate entitlements (AWS Marketplace Contract), publish a suspend message per their API and confirm response 200.
- Step 6: Monitor downstream errors for 30–60 minutes. Watch for stuck provisioning or dangling partial accounts.

Cloud-specific notes (high level):
- AWS Marketplace: Use the Seller Central "Deactivate Listing" first (hides from marketplace). If billing is affected, coordinate with finance to stop settlement for the SKU and open a case with AWS Seller Support. For entitlements, use the Entitlement-API calls to suspend.
- GCP Marketplace: Use the Private/Listing visibility toggle in Cloud Marketplace Console. For SaaS connectors, revoke OAuth tokens issued to GCP provisioning service.
- Azure Marketplace: Use the Publishing portal to unpublish; verify the Managed Application instances don't auto-provision. Contact Azure Support for billing holds if necessary.

Communication templates (short notices)
- Public partner/customer notice (short):
Subject: Temporary removal of <Listing Display Name> from our Marketplace
Body: We are temporarily removing "<Listing Display Name>" from Redwood's marketplace while we investigate an issue impacting provisioning/billing. If you have an active subscription, your service is unaffected — there is no data loss expected. For questions, contact partner-success@redwood.com. We will post updates in this thread.

- Internal support canned response:
Hi <Customer>,
Thanks for flagging this. We’ve temporarily disabled new provisioning for the marketplace listing you referenced while we investigate a billing/provisioning anomaly. Existing subscriptions remain active. We’re tracking your case internally (JIRA: <ticket>) and will update within 2 business hours.

Post-rollback validation checklist (before re-publish):
- Confirm root-cause analysis draft exists and includes the fix or mitigation plan.
- Billing reconciliation: Finance confirms no erroneous settlements or refunded invoices processing correctly.
- Security sign-off: CISO provides clearance if the rollback was security-related.
- QA sign-off: Smoke tests pass in sandbox and the canary window is defined with partial traffic.
- Partner acceptance: Partner rep signs off on re-publish timing and copy.

Re-publish gating decision matrix:
- Minor defects (non-customer-facing copy typos) -> immediate re-publish after patch.
- Moderate (edge-case provisioning failures) -> re-publish to canary first (5–10% traffic) for 24–72 hours.
- Major (billing/security/legal) -> require cross-functional approval: IC + Legal + CISO + Finance + SRE.

Post-incident tasks (owners and timeline):
- 24h: Initial customer-facing postmortem draft (Comm + IC).
- 72h: Technical RCA draft (TL + SRE).
- 7 days: Root-cause final report with remediation plan and follow-up tasks assigned to squads.
- 30 days: Verify remedial changes landed and run a simulated rollback drill for the listing.

Templates: JIRA ticket summary (use for creating incident):
- Summary: [INCIDENT] <Listing Display Name> - <primary symptom>
- Priority: P1 if customers impacted or billing issues; P2 otherwise
- Labels: marketplace, rollback, <cloud-provider>, billing
- Attach: logs, screenshots, backup artifact IDs

Legal/compliance escalation notes:
- For takedown due to intellectual property or compliance, DO NOT communicate publicly until Legal approves. Legal owner must be looped within 1 hour.

Runbook exercise guidance (quarterly):
- Runbook tabletop: simulate a billing-miscount scenario and walk through the communication cadence.
- Technical drill: SRE to perform a simulated hide/unpublish and re-publish on a non-production listing to validate steps and timing.
- Post-drill retro: capture time-to-decision, time-to-hide, and time-to-notice metrics.

Appendix: quick reference commands & links
- Seller Central (AWS): https://sellercentral.amazon.com/ (link to our org section)
- GCP Console: https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace
- Azure Publishing portal: https://partner.microsoft.com/ (marketplace publishing)
notes: Working draft. Intentionally focused on runbook mechanics and canned comms rather than full launch checklist. Will iterate with Legal and SRE for exact API call snippets and product console screenshots.
